Sometimes they speak one at a time, not separated from one another but together.
And this is the way of those whom the Lord Jesus used to send out two by two, and also of the great prophet of ancient times, Moses, and Aaron.
Sometimes Moses speaks, and sometimes Aaron speaks, while they are together.
Sometimes it is Moses who raises the staff; at other times it is Aaron who raises the staff, but not without Moses. All these things are by God's command, [?] submission according to order.
But if someone says, “These are brothers, and they are at ease about this matter, and this is how no malicious envy stirs them,”
then he is a worldly brother, not a spiritual one, concerned about his heart because of the pride that torments everyone who makes room for it within themselves.
For God's people at that time, Israel, were organized in this way, with leaders in this way over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, while holy Moses was leader over them.
